summary: A CCC stone-and-timber lookout above Ruidoso, first built in 1936 and rebuilt in 1940, now a popular (unstaffed) visitor stop on the National Register.

facts.design: CCC rustic design: 14x14 ft native stone base with living quarters, topped by a 7x7 ft metal observation cab

access.note: Reached by about 5.5 miles of Forest Service gravel/dirt road north of Ruidoso; final mile sometimes gated to vehicles (closed part of 2020, reopened by mid-2021) and the road can close in winter snow. No potable water on site.

events.note: CCC built an original lookout on the site
CCC rebuilt the lookout as the stone-base/metal-cab structure that stands today; this is the only construction date given by NHLR and Wikipedia
Listed on the National Register of Historic Places January 27, 1988 (ref 87002483), as part of the thematic nomination 'National Forest Fire Lookouts in the Southwestern Region'
Added to the New Mexico State Register of Cultural Properties March 4, 1988 (State Register No. 1445)

sources.title: Monjeau Lookout
sources.publisher: Lincoln National Forest, U.S. Forest Service

notes_for_editor: Fact-check pass (2026-10-04) found three sourcing errors, now fixed: (1) the story cited Wikipedia for the claim that the CCC built an original 1936 lookout later rebuilt in 1940, but Wikipedia only says 'completed in 1940' and never mentions 1936 — the 1936/1940 two-stage claim is supported by Living New Deal (now added as source 5) and the USFS page, not Wikipedia, which now cites only the 1940 date alongside NHLR. (2) The New Mexico State Register of Cultural Properties claim was cited to the NPGallery NRHP record, which does not mention the state register at all; that fact is supported by Wikipedia (source 2, which gives the exact date March 4, 1988 and State Register No. 1445) and has been re-cited and split into its own event. (3) The story claimed Monjeau was 'the first lookout entered into the National Historic Lookout Register' outright; NHLR's own page says only that it was 'the first NHLR listing in New Mexico' — corrected to match. Did not find the NRHP nomination PDF text itself (only the NPGallery metadata page), so architectural/material description beyond NHLR's dimensions is thinner than ideal. No source found addressing current (2026) staffing beyond the 2007 volunteer visit report, which found it unstaffed with water damage and a stalled restoration contract; NHLR's current page description separately calls the lookout 'still in active use' as a visitor destination, which is about recreational use rather than fire-watch staffing and does not contradict the 2007 report.
